# AI Image Upscaler

- Route: `/tools/ai-image-upscaler`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `ai`
- Slug: `ai-image-upscaler`

## Summary

Enlarge a small or soft photo with a Real-ESRGAN model that rebuilds fine detail instead of just stretching pixels. (AI tools)

## Details

This page opens the image converter with AI Upscale locked in and the output set to PNG. The server runs realesrgan-ncnn-vulkan, the Vulkan build of Real-ESRGAN, on a GPU we own: the default model is realesrgan-x4plus at 4x, with realesrgan-x4plus-anime and realesr-animevideov3 available for drawings and animation frames, and 2x as an alternative scale. Rather than interpolating between your existing pixels, the network predicts what edges, skin, fabric and foliage look like at the larger size and draws that detail in. The result is written as a lossless PNG so no new compression artifacts are stacked on top of the synthesized detail.
### What it does
- Enlarges an image to 2x or 4x its width and height with a Real-ESRGAN model running on our GPU.
- Lets you choose between a photo model and two anime-style models in the form; 4x and the photo model are preselected.
- Always outputs PNG; the API forces the .png extension for this operation.
- Tiles the image automatically on the GPU so large inputs do not run out of video memory.
- Spends one AI job from the daily AI allowance, a counter of its own; the everyday allowance for conversions is not touched.
### How to use it
1. Upload a small or soft image: JPG, PNG or WebP. The smaller the input, the more the model has to invent.
2. Pick 4x or 2x and a model: realesrgan-x4plus for photos, the anime models for line art and cartoon frames.
3. Real-ESRGAN runs on the GPU: realesrgan-ncnn-vulkan -i in -o out -n <model> -s <2|4> -t 0 -g <gpu> -f png
4. Download the PNG: converted.png at 2x or 4x the original pixel dimensions.
### Supported formats
- Input: jpg, jpeg, png, webp
- Output: png
- Output is PNG. Size limits and the daily AI allowance depend on your plan and are shown in the form, not fixed on this page.
### Technical details
- The call is UpscaleImage in ai_tools.go. It launches realesrgan-ncnn-vulkan with -n for the model, -s for the scale, -t 0 for automatic tile size, -g for the GPU index and -f png; the Vulkan ICD is pinned by environment variables so the loader always finds the NVIDIA driver.
- Only scales 2 and 4 and only the three model names realesrgan-x4plus, realesrgan-x4plus-anime and realesr-animevideov3 are accepted; anything else is rejected before the job starts.
- 2x runs the same x4 network at half scale. The form carries a note that 2x can look slightly cropped or zoomed on some images, which was observed on the server with a 640 x 360 photo; the API deliberately does not hide this by running 4x and downscaling.
- Because the AI path bypasses ImageMagick and the exiftool copy, the quality, resize, filter and metadata settings in the form do nothing here, and the PNG carries no EXIF from the original.
- Pixel count grows with the square of the scale: 4x means 16 times as many pixels and 2x means 4 times. The uncompressed RGB of the output is width x height x 3 bytes, which bounds how large the PNG can be.
- There is no server-side cap on input dimensions specific to this operation beyond the per-file size limit for your plan; very large inputs simply take longer, tile by tile.
### When not to use it
Do not upscale an image that is already large and sharp: a 12-megapixel photo at 4x becomes a 192-megapixel PNG that is slow to produce, hundreds of megabytes uncompressed, and gains nothing visible. Do not rely on it for faces, text, logos or anything where the exact original must be preserved, because the added detail is predicted, not recovered, and small text can come out as plausible but wrong letters. Heavy motion blur and missed focus are not fixed by resolution. If you only need a specific pixel size from a larger original, the plain resizer is faster and cheaper.
### Use cases
- Printing old photos: Take a 1-megapixel photo from an early camera to a size that prints well.
- Rescuing small downloads: Enlarge a 400 px product or reference image to something usable.
- Anime and illustration: Scale up line art with realesrgan-x4plus-anime without muddy edges.
- Game and video frames: Use realesr-animevideov3 on captured animation frames.
### FAQ
Q: Is the AI upscaler free to use?
A: Yes, within the daily AI allowance. Daily limits and file caps depend on the plan; quote them only from the live plan block. That allowance is separate from the everyday one, so your conversions are unaffected. The live numbers are on /pricing.
Q: How is this different from the image resizer?
A: The resizer runs ImageMagick, which interpolates existing pixels and makes a larger but softer image. This tool runs a trained Real-ESRGAN network that synthesizes edges and texture at the larger size. It is an inference, not recovered data.
Q: Should I pick 2x or 4x?
A: 4x is the default and gives the most consistent output. 2x runs the same network at half scale and can look slightly cropped on some images, so if 4x is more than you need, consider 4x followed by a resize down.
Q: Which model is right for drawings?
A: realesrgan-x4plus-anime for illustrations and flat-colour art; realesr-animevideov3 for frames taken from animation. The photo model adds skin-like texture that looks wrong on line art.
Q: Why is the output PNG and so large?
A: PNG is forced so the synthesized detail is not immediately damaged by JPEG compression. A 4x result has 16 times the pixels, so the file is large; compress it to JPG or WebP afterward for sharing.
Q: Can it fix a blurry or out-of-focus photo?
A: It helps with softness that comes from low resolution. It cannot undo motion blur or a missed focus, and it may smooth or alter faces and fine text. Compare the result with the original before using it.
Q: Is my photo sent to a third-party AI service?
A: No. Real-ESRGAN runs on a GPU server we operate, and the job never calls an external API.

When to send a visitor here: Send visitors here when they want a small or soft image enlarged 2x or 4x with AI-rebuilt detail rather than plain stretching: "upscale this photo", "make a low-res image bigger and sharper". Anime-style models suit drawings. Output is PNG.
When to send them elsewhere: To shrink or hit exact dimensions, use Image Resizer (image-resizer). For old, scratched or damaged photos, AI Image Restoration & Upscaling (ai-image-restoration) fits better. Not for text or logos where exact detail matters, since added detail is predicted.
